title: Template — wire shapes, version 1
description: The machine-readable half of template-v1.contract.yaml. BOTH ARE NORMATIVE TOGETHER. Nothing in this repository executes JSON Schema — no implementation, no package.json, no node_modules — so this file is normative and hand-checked, never machine-validated.

templateId.description: Opaque, server-generated, 22 characters of base64url as generated. Never chosen by a caller and never parsed by one.

templateName.description:
The business type as a human reads it: 'School', 'Dental Clinic', 'Retail'. FREE TEXT ON PURPOSE — an enum here would be the industry-noun column CORE_BOUNDARIES.md §6 rule 1 forbids, and would mean adding a business type required a code deploy. UNIQUENESS is compared after THREE steps, IN THIS ORDER: (1) REMOVE `U+200C` ZWNJ AND `U+200D` ZWJ, (2) NFKC normalisation, (3) ASCII-only case folding. Steps 2 and 3 are the credential-store.ts::normalizeIdentifier definition, restated here because that file is TypeScript and this is JSON. THE STORED AND RETURNED VALUE IS ALWAYS THE OPERATOR'S ORIGINAL, ZWNJ AND ZWJ INCLUDED — normalisation decides COLLISION, never display, which is what lets a Persian name be spelled correctly and still be unique.

*** STEP 1 IS NEW, 2026-09-10 (SR-8), AND IT MEANS `normalizeTemplateName` IS NO LONGER `normalizeIdentifier`. *** It is `normalizeIdentifier` COMPOSED WITH a strip, and Core must compose rather than modify: this contract already records why editing the shared normaliser is dangerous ('a rejection added INSIDE normalizeIdentifier, to close the identifier enforcement gap, would silently refuse every non-ASCII Template name'). The strip happens to be a no-op on an account identifier, which is printable-ASCII-only — so pushing it into the shared function would be harmless TODAY and would re-create exactly the coupling that warning is about. Leading and trailing whitespace is rejected rather than trimmed, for the reason isSubmittableIdentifier rejects rather than trims: three implementations in three languages trim different Unicode sets, and refusing removes a disagreement instead of arbitrating it.
templateName.$comment:
*** THE CHARSET RULING, 2026-09-10, AFTER SECURITY REVIEW SR-8. THE UNIQUENESS GUARANTEE WAS DEFEATED BY A TWO-CHARACTER INPUT. ***

THE DEFECT: the only constraints were a length bound and no edge whitespace. NFKC collapses fullwidth forms and DOES NOT REMOVE `U+202E` RIGHT-TO-LEFT OVERRIDE or `U+200B` ZERO WIDTH SPACE, so `School` and `Scho<U+202E>ol` normalise DIFFERENTLY, are accepted as two distinct Templates, and are VISUALLY IDENTICAL in the picker an operator chooses from. That is exactly the ambiguity template-lifecycle-v1's theALTERNATIVEREJECTED says the uniqueness index exists to prevent — the index defeated by a character it cannot see.

PRE-EXISTING, AND template-lifecycle-v1 WIDENS IT, WHICH IS WHY IT IS FIXED NOW: before PA-16 a confusable name could only be introduced at CREATION. An update route lets one be introduced into a Template ORGANIZATIONS HAVE ALREADY ADOPTED, and these strings render to every user in every adopting tenant as the name of their own structure.

=== THE RULING, IN TWO HALVES, AND THE SECOND HALF IS WHY THE FIRST CAN STAY NARROW ===

(1) REJECTED AT INPUT — by CATEGORY, not by a list of code points: Unicode general categories `Cc` (control), `Cf` (format), `Cn` (unassigned), `Co` (private use), `Zl` and `Zp` — *** WITH EXACTLY TWO EXCEPTIONS: `U+200C` ZWNJ AND `U+200D` ZWJ. *** Those two are `Cf` and are REQUIRED for correct rendering in Persian, Arabic and Indic scripts; forbidding them would refuse a legitimately-spelled name, which is the trap this contract already records for registration numbers ('a pattern is a refusal, and an at-count pattern that is wrong refuses a LEGAL registration').

STATED AS CATEGORIES DELIBERATELY. A code-point list is correct on the day it is written and silently short the next time Unicode assigns a format character; `Cf` covers one that does not exist yet. Fail-closed on a widening, which is the property architecture.md §3a-i asks for, applied to a charset.

(2) THE COLLISION KEY STRIPS THE TWO EXCEPTIONS. Uniqueness is compared after NFKC, ASCII-only case folding, AND REMOVAL OF `U+200C` AND `U+200D`. So `School` and `Scho<ZWJ>ol` COLLIDE and cannot both exist — the permitted exceptions cannot be used to build a confusable pair. THE STORED AND DISPLAYED NAME KEEPS THEM: normalisation decides COLLISION, never display, which is this contract's existing rule and is what lets a Persian name be spelled correctly and still be unique.

WHY NOT SIMPLY BAN ALL NON-ASCII: this contract already refused that, in terms — 'A TEMPLATE NAME IS NOT AN IDENTIFIER: it is a human-readable label, it legitimately contains non-ASCII, and this contract accepts that deliberately.' Dudo operates in Bahrain. An Arabic Template name is an ordinary requirement, not an edge case.

=== EXPRESSED VERSUS ENFORCED, ON BOTH AXES, BECAUSE THIS IS WHERE THAT DISTINCTION IS MOST EXPENSIVE ===

THE `pattern` ABOVE IS AN APPROXIMATION AND IS NOT THE RULE. It enumerates BMP ranges because JSON Schema patterns are ECMA-262 regexes whose `\p{...}` support is implementation-dependent, and it therefore CANNOT express the category rule and does not reach beyond the BMP. AND NOTHING IN THIS REPOSITORY EXECUTES JSON SCHEMA AT ALL. So: not covered in full (scope), and not executed (liveness) — two independent axes, workflow.md §12.

*** THE NORMATIVE RULE IS (1) AND (2) ABOVE, AND CORE ENFORCES IT AT EVERY ENTRY POINT THAT ACCEPTS A TEMPLATE NAME — create AND update. *** A reader must not conclude from the pattern that the rule is enforced, and must not conclude from the pattern's narrowness that the rule is narrow.

=== THE LENGTH BOUND IS COUNTED IN UTF-16 CODE UNITS, WHICH IS NOT WHAT `maxLength` MEANS — SR-21, 2026-09-11 ===

*** `maxLength: 80` HERE AND `40` ON `#/$defs/levelLabel` ARE ENFORCED BY `checkTemplateText` USING `value.length`, WHICH COUNTS UTF-16 CODE UNITS. JSON SCHEMA DEFINES `maxLength` IN UNICODE CODE POINTS. THE TWO DISAGREE ON EVERY ASTRAL CHARACTER. ***

An emoji, a rarer CJK extension character, an Old Persian letter — each is ONE code point and TWO code units, so it costs 2 against a bound this file states in characters. A name of 41 emoji is refused by Core and permitted by the schema. NOTHING RECONCILES THEM, because nothing in this repository executes JSON Schema: CORE'S COUNT IS THE ONE THAT RUNS, and this sentence exists so the contract does not quietly promise the other one.

IT IS NOT BEING 'FIXED', AND THE REASON IS THE SAME ONE THAT DECIDED THE CHARSET RULING. Counting code points needs `[...value].length` or an explicit iterator in three implementations that must agree byte for byte — and the bound is a UI-driven convenience, not a security property. A DISAGREEMENT ABOUT WHETHER AN 80-CHARACTER NAME IS 78 OR 80 IS NOT WORTH A RULE THREE LANGUAGES MUST SHARE. What is worth having is that the number means something specific, and it now does.

*** THIS IS THE SECOND PLACE IN THIS DEF WHERE A CONSTRAINT READ AS MORE PRECISE THAN IT IS *** — the first is the charset ruling below, which closes invisible characters and not homoglyphs. Both were found in one review. Recorded together so a reader treats the whole of this `$comment` as bounded claims rather than as a settled account of what a Template name may be.

=== WHAT THIS RULING DOES NOT COVER, AND IT MUST NOT BE QUOTED AS THOUGH IT DID — SR-16, 2026-09-11 ===

*** MIXED-SCRIPT HOMOGLYPHS ARE STILL ACCEPTED. `School` AND `Ѕсhооl` (Cyrillic `Ѕ` U+0405, `с` U+0441, `о` U+043E) ARE TWO DISTINCT TEMPLATES AND ARE VISUALLY IDENTICAL IN THE PICKER. ***

Every one of those characters is `Lu`/`Ll`, so the category rule in (1) passes them; NFKC does not map Cyrillic to Latin; ASCII-only case folding does not either — and it must stay ASCII-only, for the reason `normalizeTemplateName` gives. The joiner strip in (2) removes exactly two code points. SO THE COLLISION KEY DOES NOT COLLIDE THEM, AND THE INPUT IS EASIER THAN THE ONE THIS RULING CLOSED: no invisible character is needed, only another script's letter.

*** THE PARAGRAPHS ABOVE READ AS CLOSURE AND THAT IS THE FINDING, NOT THE GAP. *** They say the ruling closes 'exactly the ambiguity theALTERNATIVEREJECTED says the uniqueness index exists to prevent' and that 'the permitted exceptions cannot be used to build a confusable pair'. BOTH ARE TRUE OF THE EXCEPTIONS AND NEITHER IS TRUE OF CONFUSABLE PAIRS. A reader checking whether confusability is handled finds a precise, confident answer and stops — architecture.md §3b, a dismissal exact about one side and silent about the other, where the precision is what stops anyone re-deriving it.

RULED 2026-09-11: STATE THE RESIDUAL, DO NOT BUILD THE FIX. A UTS #39 skeleton or a mixed-script restriction is real work with real FALSE-REFUSAL risk in an Arabic-first market — refusing a legitimately-spelled name is the failure this contract already refuses once, in aTEMPLATENAMEISNOTANACCOUNTIDENTIFIER — this repository is zero-dependency, and the actor is one of two platform operators.

THE TRIGGER IS THE OPERATOR POPULATION, NOT A DATE: if platform operators stop being a handful of trusted people, a mixed-script restriction becomes the decision to take. Stated as the condition rather than as a verdict, so it is not read as an instruction the day a third operator is added.

NOTHING IN THIS CORPUS CONTRADICTS OR ANTICIPATES THIS. The only homoglyph reasoning anywhere is `account-identifier-v1`'s, where it is a NON-ISSUE because identifiers are printable-ASCII-only — so that argument does not transfer and must not be cited here as though it did.

CLIENT OBLIGATION, BINDING ON BOTH CLIENTS: render a Template name as TEXT, never as markup, and never wrap it in a bidi override of the client's own. A client that isolates a name for layout purposes must use `U+2068` FSI / `U+2069` PDI AROUND the value at render time and must never store or send them — they are rejected on input by (1), which is what keeps 'the client added them for layout' and 'the value contains them' distinguishable.

levelLabel.description: What a human reads in place of a structural level's internal name. IT IS A LABEL AND NOTHING ELSE: it changes no authorization, no scope, no predicate and no route. 'workspace' remains the scope identifier in permission-catalog.yaml and in the scope ladder whatever this says on screen. A label that could alter a scope would be configuration deciding authorization.
levelLabel.$comment:
*** THE SAME CHARSET RULING AS `#/$defs/templateName`, SR-8, 2026-09-10. THE FULL ARGUMENT IS THERE AND IS NOT REPEATED; WHAT IS BELOW IS WHAT DIFFERS. ***

*** AND THE SAME TWO LIMITS APPLY, BOTH ARGUED ON `templateName` AND NEITHER REPEATED: `maxLength: 40` IS COUNTED BY CORE IN UTF-16 CODE UNITS RATHER THAN IN CODE POINTS (SR-21), AND THE CHARSET RULING DOES NOT COVER MIXED-SCRIPT HOMOGLYPHS (SR-16). *** They land differently here. THE HOMOGLYPH RESIDUAL IS SMALLER ON THIS DEF — a level label has no uniqueness comparison, so there is no confusable PAIR to construct. THE LENGTH LIMIT IS THE SAME SIZE: a label of 21 emoji is refused against a bound that reads as 40 characters, and these strings are interpolated into sentences a tenant's own staff read.

REJECTED AT INPUT by category — `Cc`, `Cf`, `Cn`, `Co`, `Zl`, `Zp` — with exactly two exceptions, `U+200C` ZWNJ and `U+200D` ZWJ, which Persian, Arabic and Indic scripts require. The `pattern` above is a BMP approximation of that rule and is neither complete nor executed; CORE ENFORCES THE CATEGORY RULE at every entry point that accepts a level label, which is create AND update.

*** WHAT DIFFERS HERE, AND IT MAKES THE CASE STRONGER RATHER THAN WEAKER: A LEVEL LABEL HAS NO UNIQUENESS COMPARISON AT ALL. *** templateName's second half — strip ZWNJ and ZWJ from the collision key — HAS NO EQUIVALENT, because nothing compares two level labels. So the confusability argument that drove the ruling there does not apply here, AND THE RULING STILL DOES, for a different reason:

THESE STRINGS ARE RENDERED TO EVERY USER IN EVERY ADOPTING TENANT AS THE NAME OF THEIR OWN STRUCTURE. A `U+202E` here reverses the rendering of whatever follows it in a navigation label, on a screen belonging to a customer who never chose the Template and cannot edit it. THE INJECTION POINT IS A PLATFORM OPERATOR AND THE BLAST RADIUS IS EVERY ADOPTER — and template-lifecycle-v1's update route is what makes it reach adopters who are ALREADY LIVE rather than only future ones.

SO THE TWO DEFS SHARE A RULE AND NOT A REASON. Recorded that way deliberately: if the uniqueness comparison on templateName is ever changed, this def must NOT be swept along with it, and if these labels ever acquire a comparison, this note is what tells the next author that the missing half was absent rather than forgotten.

CLIENT OBLIGATION, BINDING ON BOTH CLIENTS, AND IT MATTERS MORE HERE THAN ON A NAME: render a level label as TEXT, never as markup. A label is interpolated into sentences a user reads ('which of your Campuses is this filed under'), so it reaches more rendering paths than a name shown in a list does. Bidi isolation at render time uses `U+2068`/`U+2069` around the value and is never stored or sent — those are rejected on input, which is what keeps 'the client added them' and 'the value contains them' distinguishable.

levelLabels.description: A CLOSED SET OF EXACTLY THREE KEYS, one per structural level Dudo has. Not a free-form map: an open map would let an operator invent a level that does not exist, and a client rendering an unknown key would be drawing a structure the platform does not have. `team` is absent deliberately — it is a first-class object with its own name and no per-type variation anyone has asked for. `own` and `resource` are absent because they are authorization scopes, not places. Every key is OPTIONAL and an absent one takes the platform default below.

organization.description: A school group renders 'Group', a clinic 'Practice', a company 'Company'. This is the half of the naming collision that is solved by a label rather than by a rename: the user's word for the tenant is 'business', and serving it here costs no schema change to the most embedded identifier in the platform.

workspace.description: A school renders 'Campus', a shop 'Branch', a clinic 'Site'. THE KEY IS `workspace`, AND TWO VOCABULARIES FOR THIS LEVEL COEXIST DELIBERATELY: the new platform surface says `Workspace`, the customer wire and the database say `business_id`, and neither is to be corrected toward the other. CORRECTED 2026-09-05 — this previously said the schema would be WRONG if the rename were deferred. The rename IS deferred, and not for indecision: docs/decisions/0025's Amendment established that `business_id` is a published wire field two clients have shipped against and a persisted audit value, so renaming it is a breaking change plus an audit-history rewrite, owed to its own slice with a closing trigger (before a second App ships a contract using the word). THE COEXISTENCE IS THE DECISION, NOT A FAILURE STATE. And note that these labels are what the user actually asked for: the complaint was about words on a screen, and a school rendering 'Campus' fixes it today with no breaking change.

branch.description: The level below a Workspace. Unchanged by the rename, and the reason `Branch` was unavailable as the new name for the inner unit: it already names a level below it.

enumPolicyDivergence.reason: Response versus request direction. docs/decisions/0041 amendment 1.

templateStatus.description:
THE STATUS A CLIENT READS. Declared with both values.

*** THIS FIELD'S OWN HISTORY IS THE ONE TO GET RIGHT, AND IT HAS A TRIGGER RATHER THAN A DATE. *** It previously read 'NO ROUTE SETS IT ... every Template is active forever; retirement is TM-2.' THAT IS STILL TRUE OF THE DEPLOYED SYSTEM AND STOPS BEING TRUE WHEN template-lifecycle-v1's retire route LANDS — not when that contract was authored, and not when it was accepted. Whoever ships the route owes this sentence an edit. Stated as a trigger because a sentence about a missing capability outlives the capability arriving, and every reader who quotes this one will be quoting it for the half that is still true (workflow.md §12).

WHY `extensible` SURVIVES THE ROUTE ARRIVING RATHER THAN BEING SETTLED BY IT: a third status is plausible — a `draft` a Template sits in before it may be adopted is the obvious one — and 0041's tolerant-client argument stops being hypothetical the day `retired` becomes reachable, because that is the first day a client can meet a status it was not built for.
templateStatus.$comment: ONE VOCABULARY, TWO POLICIES, BOTH CORRECT — see `#/$defs/templateStatusFilter`, which carries the identical value set and is `closed`. THE DUPLICATE-POLICY CHECK IS EXPECTED TO FLAG THIS PAIR AND IS WRONG TO, which is the single case docs/decisions/0041 amendment 1 identifies. `enumPolicyDivergence` above is the declared exemption; read it there, not here.

enumPolicyDivergence.reason: Request versus response direction. docs/decisions/0041 amendment 1.

templateStatusFilter.description:
THE STATUS A CLIENT SENDS, as an optional filter on platform.templates.list. ABSENT MEANS UNFILTERED — both statuses, which is exactly today's behaviour, so adding this parameter changes nothing for a caller that ignores it.

*** `closed` BECAUSE IT IS A REQUEST, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE RULE. *** docs/decisions/0041 amendment 1: `extensible` is a claim about what the SERVER sends, so a request enum is always `closed`. There is no direction in which a client may filter on a status the server has never heard of — the tolerant reading would have Core accepting an unrecognised value from a caller and choosing what to do with it, which is not tolerance but a validation hole. An unlisted value is invalid_argument.

*** NO `all` MEMBER, AND THE ABSENCE IS DELIBERATE ON TWO COUNTS. *** Unfiltered is expressed by omitting the parameter, which is the ordinary meaning of an absent filter and needs no vocabulary. AND ADDING `all` WOULD HAVE MADE THIS A DIFFERENT VALUE SET FROM `templateStatus`, which would have quietly dodged the duplicate-policy check rather than exercising it. This pair is the deliberate live instance, and it is shaped so the check CAN see it.

*** A CORRECTION TO WHAT THIS SENTENCE ORIGINALLY SAID, 2026-09-09. *** It cited customer-directory-v1's `statusFilter`/`customerStatus` as 'the same accident, where a single extra member is the only reason the check stays green on a pair it would otherwise have flagged.' THAT WAS WRONG: BOTH of those defs are `closed`, so the check finds agreement and would have been green with or without `all`. There is no divergence there to hide. The near-miss is PROSPECTIVE rather than current — it becomes real only if `customerStatus` is ever made `extensible` — and it is recorded on both of those defs.

AND `all` IS LOAD-BEARING THERE, WHICH IS THE OTHER HALF OF THE CORRECTION: that filter declares `default: "active"`, so absence means `active` rather than unfiltered and 'every state' is unexpressible without naming a value. THIS filter has no default and could not have one — it was added to an already-published list route, and changing a published default is breaking. THE TWO SHAPES DIFFER BECAUSE THE ROUTES WERE PUBLISHED AT DIFFERENT TIMES, not because one is tidier.
templateStatusFilter.$comment: NORMATIVE CLIENT RULE, BINDING ON BOTH CLIENTS: an operator-facing list of Templates SENDS `status=active` BY DEFAULT. The server default is unfiltered and is not changing — a published operation's behaviour is not altered under callers that have shipped — so the correct default lives in the client, where it is a presentation decision, and it is stated in the contract so the two clients do not choose differently. A picker offering a retired Template beside an active one recreates the 'indistinguishable to the operator choosing one' defect that name-uniqueness exists to prevent, one field along.

createTemplateInput.$comment:
*** IF YOU ARE HERE TO ADD THE `apps` FIELD, READ THIS FIRST. TWO PERMISSION SENSITIVITIES ARE OWED A REVISIT AND NEITHER WILL ANNOUNCE ITSELF. ***

The `apps` list is DEFERRED, NOT FORBIDDEN — the description below says so, and template-lifecycle-v1's theBoundary says a Template 'MAY NAME Apps AND CARRY LABELS'. So this is a field that is EXPECTED TO ARRIVE, and every sensitivity argument in the permission catalogue currently rests on a Template carrying NOTHING BUT LABELS.

  core.platform-organization.set-template — its proposal already records the trigger: 'IF A TEMPLATE EVER CARRIES ANYTHING BUT LABELS, THIS RUNG IS THE FIRST THING TO REVISIT.'
  core.template.update — *** RECORDED NOWHERE UNTIL 2026-09-10, AND IT IS THE LARGER OF THE TWO. *** With an apps list, editing a Template changes WHICH Apps every adopting Organization has. set-template reaches ONE Organization per call; update reaches EVERY ADOPTER IN ONE CALL. Its `sensitive` rung was argued on 'a label alters no scope', and an installed App is not a label.

WHY THE NOTE IS HERE RATHER THAN IN THE CATALOGUE: the person adding the field is reading THIS shape, not three files away in permission-catalog.yaml, and a trigger stored where nobody stands is a trigger nobody trips. architecture.md §3a — the guard belongs where the act happens.

A SENSITIVITY REVISIT IS A SECURITY DECISION AND GOES TO security-agent. It is not a consequence an implementer may absorb while adding a field.
createTemplateInput.description: NOTE WHAT CANNOT BE SENT: no template_id (server-generated), no status (always active), no apps list (deferred — there is one App, so the field would have one possible value and would have to be designed against an installation mechanism that does not exist), and no role labels (deferred to AZ11 — shipping them would look like it addressed the parent case, AZ10, and would not).

templateOutput.$comment:
*** IF YOU ARE ADDING A FIELD THAT IS NOT A LABEL — an `apps` list is the expected one — TWO PERMISSION SENSITIVITIES ARE OWED A REVISIT: `core.template.update` AND `core.platform-organization.set-template`. *** The full argument is on `#/$defs/createTemplateInput`, and it is restated here rather than cross-referenced because a field arrives in BOTH shapes and a reader editing the response half may never open the request half.

THE ONE-LINE VERSION: every `sensitive` rung on a Template permission was argued on 'a Template carries labels and nothing else'. An installed App is not a label, and `core.template.update` reaches every adopting Organization in a single call.
templateOutput.description: level_labels is ALWAYS FULLY POPULATED in a response, with defaults filled in for any key the operator omitted. The client therefore never implements the default table, which is what stops the web and Apple clients drifting into two different ideas of what an unlabelled level is called.

templateCountOutput.description: How many Templates exist. The number `platform.templates.list` cannot state, because a paginated list can only say 'at least 25' until its last page.

total.description: The number of rows in the `template` table, BOTH STATUSES. It is not filtered by `templateStatusFilter` and takes no query parameter: a total that changed with a filter would be a different number under the same name, and the operator asking 'how many Templates are there' is asking about the table. ZERO IS VALID AND REACHABLE — no Template has been created yet. IT MUST BE A COUNT AND NEVER A FETCH-AND-LENGTH.

templateCountOutput.$comment:
*** A SCALAR AND NOTHING ELSE. `additionalProperties: false` IS THE ENFORCEMENT OF THAT RULE AND NOT TIDINESS. *** docs/decisions/0042. No breakdown, no grouping, no count-by-status map: each transposes into a MAPPING, and the mapping is what docs/decisions/0028 Decision 1 refuses.

*** WHY THIS COUNT NEEDS NO PERMISSION OF ITS OWN WHILE THE ADOPTION COUNT NEEDED ONE — READ THIS BEFORE CONCLUDING THE TWO RULINGS DISAGREE. ***

security.md §2a: a count is safe exactly when its consumer already holds ENUMERATION over the counted population, and dangerous exactly when it does not.

  THIS COUNT counts TEMPLATES, and `core.template.list` holders enumerate Templates. It reaches nothing past their enumeration right — walking the pages yields the same number, more slowly and at an audit row per page.

  `organizations_using` COUNTS ORGANIZATIONS, and `core.template.list` grants NOTHING over the Organization population. That count reaches PAST its consumer's enumeration right, which is why it has its own `sensitive` permission — `core.template-adoption.read` — rather than sitting in this family.

*** SAME FAMILY, DIFFERENT POPULATIONS, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE DIFFERENCE. *** A reader meeting two counts in `core.template.*` should not have to re-derive this from two contracts. Permissions are granted by FAMILY: anyone composing a role that 'can read Templates' reaches for `core.template.*`, and the adoption count is deliberately NOT in it for exactly that reason.

SHAPED THE SAME AS `urn:dudo:schema:platform-operator:1#/$defs/organizationCountOutput` AND DELIBERATELY NOT SHARED WITH IT — same shape by coincidence, not by rule. See that def for why coupling them would be the harmonising mistake.

next_cursor.description: Opaque. Never constructed or parsed by a client. Null means no further page.
